newsitem.title: USA: Crestar Financial ends stock buyback plan.
newsitem.headline: Crestar Financial ends stock buyback plan.

text.p: Crestar Financial Corp said on Tuesday it has rescinded its stock repurchase plan after the Securities and Exchange Commission informed Crestar that its repurchases are not a systematic plan.
The shares repurchased under the plan were to be used for dividend reinvestment, profit sharing and stock compensation plans, Crestar said in a statement.
A total of 223,750 common shares had previously been purchased under the two million share authorization.

Related to the SEC staff decision, Crestar has rescinded the remaining February 1997 authorization and further will not acquire or authorize the acquisition of any common stock until after December 31, 1998.

The practical effect of this development is that the corporation will not buy back any shares for the dividend reinvestment or employee benefit plans or to reduce the number of shares outstanding, Crestar said.
Acquisitions using stock, however, will be generally permitted, if it is accounted for by the purchase method.
The company was not immediately available for further comment.

A Crestar spokesman later said the Securities and Exchange Commission raised the issue about the stock repurchases, because of accounting rules that apply to recent acquisitions that are accounted for as poolings of interest.
The spokesman said the repurchase program did not meet the commission's definition of the word "systematic."

Crestar elected to stop the repurchase program, because it could have led to the restatement of earnings related to its acquisition of Citizens Bancorp, which was accounted for as a pooling of interest, the spokesman said. Crestar does not have any immediate plans to appeal the Securities and Exchange Commission's findings, the spokesman said.
